answer: Each epoch an identity seals a commitment to a bid, then reveals after the window closes. Payout is split across every co-revealing identity sharing the same commitment hash, so a thousand clones behind one pledge divide one share a thousand ways. A lone participant who commits independently takes a full share. Cloning dilutes its own payout, and distinct commitments cost a fresh stake per hash, burned if the reveal is late. The comet of cloned bids collapses into a reef of mutually diluting claims, and the only profitable vertex is one that commits, reveals, and stands apart.
